question: In 2025, Saudi Arabia signed a major security agreement with which country to strengthen military cooperation amid regional tensions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, **Saudi Arabia** and **Pakistan** signed a significant security agreement aimed at deepening their **bilateral military cooperation** and strategic partnership.
 
• The agreement focuses on enhancing **joint military exercises**, sharing **intelligence**, and collaborating on **counter-terrorism** operations to address evolving regional security challenges.
 
• A major component of this pact involves **Defense Industrial Cooperation**, where both nations agreed to explore joint ventures in **defense production** and the transfer of **military technology**.
 
• The security pact also emphasizes **maritime security** in the **Arabian Sea** and the **Indian Ocean**, ensuring the safety of vital **international sea lanes** and trade routes.
 
• This collaboration is seen as a move to stabilize the **Middle East** and **South Asia** regions, reflecting the high level of trust between the **Saudi Armed Forces** and the **Pakistan Armed Forces**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Defense Ties:** The security relationship between **Saudi Arabia** and **Pakistan** dates back several decades, formally strengthened by a **defense protocol** signed in **1982**. Under this framework, **Pakistan** has historically provided **military training** and advisory services to the **Saudi military**.
 
• **Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition (IMCTC):** Both nations are prominent members of the **IMCTC**, a 41-nation alliance headquartered in **Riyadh**. The coalition, often led by retired high-ranking officers from **Pakistan**, focuses on **counter-terrorism** through four domains: ideology, communications, counter-terrorist financing, and military.
 
• **Strategic Location:** **Saudi Arabia** views **Pakistan** as a key strategic ally due to its location at the crossroads of **Central Asia**, **China**, and the **Middle East**. Conversely, **Saudi Arabia** is the **"Heart of the Islamic World"** and a major energy supplier for **Pakistan**.
 
• **Joint Exercises:** The two countries regularly conduct high-intensity military drills such as **Al-Samsaam** (army), **Al-Kassah** (anti-explosive/mine), and **Naseem Al-Bahr** (navy) to improve **interoperability** between their respective forces.
 
• **Economic and Security Synergy:** The security agreement often runs parallel to economic initiatives like the **Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC)** in **Pakistan**, which encourages **Saudi investment** in sectors like **mining**, **agriculture**, and **information technology**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regional Stability:** The **2025 agreement** is particularly relevant given the shifting **geopolitical dynamics** in the **Gulf region** and the need for a unified approach toward **non-state actors** and **maritime piracy**.
 
• **Humanitarian and Peacekeeping:** Beyond combat operations, the pact includes provisions for **disaster management** and cooperation in **United Nations Peacekeeping** missions where both countries are active contributors.
 
• **Cybersecurity:** Modern security challenges including **cyber warfare** and **digital surveillance** were also integrated into the **2025 framework**, marking an evolution from traditional kinetic warfare to modern **hybrid security** needs.
